record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: dynamical interpretation of two-dimensional BEC radii
record.original_question: In two-dimensional Bose-Einstein-correlation analysis, where pion correlations are analyzed in the Longitudinal Centre of Mass System using longitudinal and transverse momentum-difference variables to determine a longitudinal emitter dimension r_L and transverse dimension r_T, to what extent is it valid to infer the underlying dynamics of heavy-ion collisions from r_L(m_T) when the same longitudinal-radius dependence on transverse mass m_T appears in electron-positron annihilations, which contain no nuclear matter?

evidence.quote: In recent years the correlations of pions emerging from heavy ion collisions and from e+e− annihilations have been analysed in terms of the 2-dimensional BEC analysis. This analysis is carried out in the Longitudinal Centre of Mass System

From a fit to the data one is able to determine the longitudinal rL and the transverse rT dimensions. The dependence of rL on mT are shown in Fig. 3 for e+e− annihilations, as measured by DELPHI at the Z0 mass, and for S+Pb collisions at 200 GeV/A as measured by the NA44 collaboration.

At this point the obvious question arises as to what extend one is permitted to extract from the 2-dimensional BEC analyses information on the underlying dynamics of heavy ion collisions when rL(mT) behaves essentially the same as the in e+e− annihilations which are void of nuclear matter.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-particle Bose–Einstein correlations of identical pions produced in high-energy collisions. For each pair of identical pions with four-momenta p_1 and p_2, define the momentum difference Q = p_1 − p_2 and decompose it in the Longitudinal Centre of Mass System (the frame in which the longitudinal pair momentum vanishes) into a longitudinal component Q_L (along the collision axis) and a transverse component Q_T. Also define the transverse mass of the pair by m_T = sqrt(m_pi^2 + k_T^2), where k_T is the transverse component of the pair's average momentum and m_pi is the pion mass.

Model the two-pion correlation function in the form
   C_2(Q_L, Q_T) = 1 + lambda · exp(− r_L^2 Q_L^2 − r_T^2 Q_T^2),
where lambda ∈ [0,1] is an incoherence parameter and r_L, r_T ≥ 0 are the longitudinal and transverse emitter dimensions, both regarded as functions of m_T.

Empirically, the function r_L(m_T) extracted from electron–positron annihilations at the Z^0 mass (a system containing no nuclear matter) is essentially the same as the r_L(m_T) extracted from heavy-ion collisions such as S+Pb at 200 GeV per nucleon.

Question: To what extent, and under what additional assumptions on the emission source, is it justified to interpret the measured dependence r_L(m_T) in heavy-ion collisions as encoding the underlying nuclear-collision dynamics (e.g. longitudinal expansion, freeze-out time, collective flow), given that the same dependence arises in a hadronic system in which no nuclear matter is present? Formulate criteria — in terms of source models, space–time emission distributions, and the relationship between r_L(m_T) and dynamical parameters — that would allow such a dynamical inference to be made unambiguously, or show that no such criteria exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a foundational interpretational/open question regarding the dynamical meaning of longitudinal BEC radii. A definitive resolution does not appear in the literature; subsequent BEC studies in e+e- and heavy-ion contexts continue to discuss this puzzle without settling it. Status remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bose-Einstein correlations review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews of BEC continue to discuss the similarity of m_T dependence between e+e- and heavy-ion systems as an unresolved interpretational issue.
status_evidence.claim: Similarity of r_L(m_T) across systems remains an open interpretational issue.
